    EasyCrypt's programmable random oracles (theories/crypto/PROM.ec), FullRO #

    The abstract theory FullRO's types in_t, out_t, d_in_t, d_out_t and its operator dout are section variables, so a clone is an application. Only what ported developments use is here: the module types, MainD, the oracles RO, LRO, FRO and FullEager.RRO, and the statement of FullEager.RO_LRO_D.

    Translation notes (see notes/SHA3/README.md):

    • EasyCrypt's module type and module RO share a name, as do FRO and FRO; the module types are RO_T and FRO_T (exception E3 of the SHA-3 port).
    • module RO : RO, ROmap has both types: it is declared at ROmap (the larger), and RO.asRO is its RO_T view.
    • proc init = RO.init (a procedure alias) is the same procedure: LRO and RRO are assembled with RO_T.mk/FRO_T.mk from the procedures they share.
    • The module variables RO.m, FRO.m are parameters: each clone declares its own global_vars (F.RO.m, F2.RO.m …) and passes them.

        What is derivable about the accessor RO_T.init, bundled into one ModuleTypeUtilities (one name per field in the namespace, rather than one per fact):

          def GaudisCrypt.EC.PROM.FullRO.RO_T (in_t out_t : Type) :
          Type 1

          The module type declared by moduletype RO_T, with fields init, get, set, rem, sample: the type Module RO_T.typeRep of modules that are a right-nested tuple of the field types.

          Build one from a record of its fields with RO_T.mk, read a single field off one with the accessors RO_T.init, RO_T.get, RO_T.set, RO_T.rem, RO_T.sample, and get the whole record back with RO_T.structure.

            source
            @[simp]
            theorem GaudisCrypt.EC.PROM.FullRO.RO_T.set.mk_simp (in_t out_t : Type) (theRecord✝ : Structure in_t out_t) :
            set in_t out_t (mk in_t out_t theRecord✝) = theRecord✝.set

            @[simp]: reading the field set back off a module built from a record — RO_T.set (RO_T.mk r) = r.set.

            It is what carries the right-hand side of an X.apply_simp (which is an RO_T.mk) on to the field the caller actually asked for, so that simp chains X.apply_simp into X.set.apply_simp.

            noncomputable def GaudisCrypt.EC.PROM.FullRO.RO_T.set (in_t out_t : Type) :
            RO_T in_t out_t → procmod (in_t, out_t) → Unit

            The field set of a module of type RO_T: the projection onto component 2 of the right-nested tuple RO_T.typeRep, as a chain of Module.fst'/Module.snd'. Tagged @[module_accessor].

            RO_T.set.mk_simp reads this field back off a module built by RO_T.mk; RO_T.set.utilities has the accessor as a module, and the lemmas about it.

            Its parameters are named x, y, in that order (recorded in @[gaudiProcParamNames], a ProcedureSignature holding only their types).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    EC's FullEager.RO_LRO_D, for declare module D <: RO_Distinguisher {-RO, -FRO} and axiom dout_ll x : is_lossless (dout x): equiv[ D(RO).distinguish ~ D(LRO).distinguish : ={glob D, RO.m, arg} ==> ={res, glob D} ]. RO.m and FRO.m are distinct variables, and the oracles' arguments countable (exception E8). EC's proof: two transitivitys through M.main1 = RRO.resample(); D(FRO) and M.main2 = D(RRO); RRO.resample(), by RO_FRO_D, eager_D and LRO_RRO_D.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    D's procedure may have any signature, not only RO_Distinguisher's procmod (d_in_t) → d_out_t: EC's proc distinguish() with d_in_t = unit is procmod () → … here, which is not procmod (Unit) → … (an alias proc distinguish = D(…).distinguish has the callee's).
